requirements.requirement: Explicit system scope, domains, instances, environment and build identity
Separate actual application limits, analysis bounds and abstraction
Construct and confirm multiple business/state/rule networks with explicit interactions
Model-driven questions, role-aware review, authority, evidence and invalidation
Recalled modeling obligations and automatic reconciliation in each coding batch
Strict versioned JSON and one canonical owner for every definition
Source, probe and state/action correspondence across languages
Separate intent, mapping, capture, business, model and project reports
Optional finite analysis and source-linked counterexamples
Readable, isolated modules and minimal application coupling
Model overview, progressive graph inspection, truthful replay and preserved views

cases.case: Product, architect, developer and mixed-role respondents; skip/change preference
cases.expected: Equivalent underlying meaning with suitable wording. No inferred authority, forced profiling or unnecessary technical quiz. Preserve actual dialogue.

cases.case: Human intent, technical choice, source fact and analysis assumption in one iteration
cases.expected: Route to the right owner/stage. Implementation facts require source/test evidence. An agent recommendation cannot become a user confirmation.

cases.case: More than three ambiguities, partial answers, dependencies, silence and a contradiction
cases.expected: Small per-round batches; all remaining issues retained. Only affected scope waits. Existing valid answers reused and changed answers preserved in history.

cases.case: Unknown fields/versions, missing refs, type errors, conflicting owners, missing frame conditions
cases.expected: Strict schema/semantic rejection with stable codes/paths. A source-free draft stays inspectable; invalid bound definitions do not load.

cases.case: Unbounded IDs, strings, queues, collection contents, clocks and counters
cases.expected: Finite admission finds each unbounded dimension. Numeric bounds alone do not certify arbitrary numbers; live-instance limits do not bound generated identity history.

cases.case: Analysis cap differs from application capacity; sampled and abstracted values
cases.expected: Application behavior stays unchanged. Result records bound origin and abstraction justification. Do not generalize under-approximated exploration.

cases.case: Several independent models with identical local names/instance IDs
cases.expected: No identity collision or fabricated joining edges. Every model remains queryable, bound and covered after an unrelated model changes.

cases.case: Grant revocation interleaves with a queued download
cases.expected: Check the trial's confirmed rule at its declared native boundary. Wrong read timing produces a business/property failure even if mapping is accurate.

cases.case: Shared capacity, waiting, join, cancel, retry and resource release
cases.expected: Real barriers expose competing invocations. Capacity and join membership remain scoped correctly; leaked resources/early joins are detected. Unsupported engine semantics fail admission.

cases.case: Restart/initial-state alternatives, duplicate/lost/reordered messages and external failures when applicable
cases.expected: Each selected environmental behavior is explicit. An impossible/empty initial model fails; service quiescence and intended termination are not misreported as defects.

cases.case: One concept maps to several calls; an internal call leaves abstract state unchanged
cases.expected: Correct value mapping and completion evidence, with separate call identities. Do not invent concept duration or state changes from mere containment.

cases.case: Observer off, unavailable, failing, queue-limited and optional TLC absent
cases.expected: Same authoritative business effects and native state transitions. Report capture gaps. Viewer, polling, recording and analysis operations produce no business events.

cases.case: Successful/denied/error HTTP responses, early returns, exceptions and detached callbacks
cases.expected: Actual framework status and lifecycle closure captured. Internal facts retain real invocation ownership; no synthetic return events.

cases.case: Add a handler, background job, state write and data effect without adding graph nodes
cases.expected: Independent scan detects each missing mapping/obligation. Existing-graph traversal alone cannot satisfy the case.

cases.case: Remove one return probe, alter a captured parameter, omit a native transition/commit witness
cases.expected: Protected checks fail for the relevant missing or wrong fact. Retain actual invalid runtime data and exact error path.

cases.case: Move a file, split a handler, change an async callback, then change a shared rule
cases.expected: Technical rebind happens without redundant business questioning. Shared dependents are rechecked. No stale source/doc/probe references remain.

cases.case: Skip recall/scan; switch host; resume after interruption; narrow a check to bypass failure
cases.expected: Persistent obligations remain discoverable and acceptance rejects unprocessed revisions or weakened scope. Explicit activation remains chat/project scoped.

cases.case: Correct graph mapping of a real business bug, then incorrect mapping of correct business behavior
cases.expected: Reports distinguish mapping, capture, state rules, business and project results. Neither outcome hides the other's failure.

cases.case: Small manually understood finite model through actual TLC; a deliberately broken transition
cases.expected: Expected property result and counterexample. Compare with independently authored TLA fixtures and hand-derived reachable states. Identify design versus implementation analysis; a correct design pass must not conceal a failing native implementation.

cases.case: Timeout, unsupported expression, missing tool, stale profile, incomplete traversal and invariant used as a filter
cases.expected: No false pass. Detect vacuous/filtered verification and preserve failed/partial runs. A changed compiler/profile/property invalidates the result.

cases.case: Model counterexample and real reproduction shown in Graph/Timeline
cases.expected: Distinct provenance; model uses logical steps, real run uses actual intervals. Stable IDs, values, cross-model paths and a liveness loop witness remain inspectable.

cases.case: Progress property with/without supported fairness and an external outcome assumption
cases.expected: Show exactly which assumption the result depends on. No automatic fairness insertion; unsupported temporal semantics are explicit.

cases.case: Legacy migration, interrupted writes, rollback, overlapping IDs, stale writers and export/import
cases.expected: Existing gates preserved; mixed revisions rejected; IDs, accepted meaning, personal views and archived evidence survive.

cases.case: Architecture, source comments, dependency inventory and managed copies
cases.expected: No analysis/viewer engine in application bundles; thin adapters; readable ownership and docstrings; no hand-edited installed copies.

cases.case: Desktop 2D/3D, custom filters, hidden layers, expansion, drag, recording, replay and Timeline
cases.expected: Correct typed relations, visible flow feedback and lifetimes; camera/layout/annotations retained after update; English/Chinese names reflect locale.

cases.case: Homepage/demo story and loading
cases.expected: Concise benefit-led copy; matching first/last graph definitions; focused prepared scenes; no prolonged full-graph filtering between scenes. Existing loading/browser regressions pass.

cases.case: Python drive and Node observe, plus existing reverse-mode adapter coverage and React/Vue entry fixtures
cases.expected: Same JSON meaning and evidence requirements. Actual async handoff, database completion and API errors work; unsupported framework paths remain explicit.

cases.case: Fresh dialogue trial, business iteration, source-only refactor and clean exported package
cases.expected: Full question/design/build/observe/change/retest record; framework fixes retested from a fresh installation; complete final run after the last fix.

cases.case: Source-free request containing several capabilities, state-owning objects and shared decisions
cases.expected: Inventory and independent business/state/rule network views match the stated scope. Preserve legitimate independent components, loops and shared predicate identity; no forced common route.

cases.case: Omit a stated capability, state owner, branch or applicable cross-model effect before authoring any question
cases.expected: Source-backed modeling obligations expose the omission. Missing-model construction targets survive until valid drafts exist; executable validation stays strict. An empty question list or containment-only graph cannot close the gap.

cases.case: Review the same model scope with product, architecture and development respondents; use grouped cards and ordinary chat
cases.expected: Equivalent confirmed semantics, stable IDs and complete applicable obligations. Conditional answers, partial responses, role changes and restart preserve one decision history; the agent resolves implementation facts.

cases.case: Show only part of a model, hide a shared rule dependency, then change the draft before receiving an answer
cases.expected: Confirmation applies only to actually reviewed matching meaning. Omitted boundaries stay explicit; stale presentation cannot confirm a newer semantic snapshot. Clear overview and boundary views use the same graph IDs.

cases.case: Add an independent capability; split/retire a model; discover an unmodeled source behavior; change a shared rule
cases.expected: Reconcile inventory and intent basis, review missing meaning and all affected consumers, refresh bindings/probes/cases, retain unrelated models/views. A source-only refactor does not trigger redundant intent questions.

cases.case: Complete multi-network trial through model review, native binding, observation, iteration and product scene export
cases.expected: Every in-scope model/boundary has its applicable static and runtime evidence. Hidden networks retain obligations. Analysis includes relevant boundary assumptions; initial and later demo graphs use the same accepted definitions.
